newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks edge lower before July jobs data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks edge lower before July jobs data.

text.p: Stocks edged lower on Thursday after seesawing for much of day as financial markets were jittery ahead of a key July employment report due out Friday.
At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was off 0.23 points at 8,254.66, after opening higher.
In the broader market, advancing issues outpaced decliners by a 15-to-11 margin on volume of about 322 million on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq composite index edged up 3.55 points to 1,591.60.

"The market is waiting for tomorrow's employment number," said Peter Coolidge, senior equity trader at Brean Murray & Co. "The market has had a really decent run this week, with lots of positive momentum in both the credit and equity markets. But we are taking a little bit of a breather here."

The July employment data due on Friday is scrutinised because it offers the first glimpse into the economy's performance during the third quarter, analysts said. The data has shaken both bond and stock markets in the past.
"I expect the market to walk in place or even give back ground until we get information on the employment number," said Charles White, managing director at Avatar Associates.
The jobless rate was expected to dip to 4.9 percent, with nonfarm payrolls rising by 193,000.
On Thursday, financial markets were also buffeted by second-quarter gross domestic product data, weekly jobless claims and the Chicago Purchasing Managers report.
A benign 2.2 percent annualized rise in GDP during the second quarter, combined with a very small rise in the price deflator, initially boosted stocks and bonds.
The deflator -- which showed its smallest gain since 1964 -- initially calmed the bond market's inflationary fears.
But markets tripped after the Chicago Purchasing Managers index came at a surprisingly strong 60.6 in July vs. a forecast of 59.8.
But analysts said the increase in its prices paid component was more disturbing to markets.

"The bond market in particular seemed to weaken after the Chicago PMI report, and stocks followed suit," Greg Nie, a technical analyst at Everen Securities, said. "Today's data was more on the confusing side than anything else."
Stocks also digested weekly jobless claims, which fell to 277,000 in the latest week, and the help-wanted ad index.
The Conference Board said its U.S. help-wanted advertising index rose 7 points in June to an 88.0 reading. The group said the U.S. labour market was expanding "about as fast as it possibly could."

Among individual stocks, Wendy's International Inc. slid 2-3/8 to 24-7/8 after the fast-food company reported lower second-quarter earnings and said its second-half sales would be hurt by rising labour and raw material costs and a higher tax rate. Merrill Lynch and Smith Barney both downgraded Wendy's stock.
True North Communications Inc.'s stock rose 13/16 to 23-7/8 after it signed a definitive agreement to acquire Bozell, Jacobs, Kenyon and Eckhardt Inc. in a deal valued at about $440 million.
